title: Ops Reactor: evented action catalog + idempotent runbook adapter
creator: Luca Morgan
description: Implement a small, event-driven service (Ops Reactor) and an Action Catalog that turns existing runbook steps into reusable 'actionlets' which can be executed as tasks by the support UI or invoked by automation. Focus is on safe, idempotent execution of side-effecting steps, step-level tracing for cost/latency attribution, and a lightweight governance model (approval gates, dry-run mode). This ticket scopes the core runtime, the schema for actionlets (v1), and an adapter that converts current runbook YAML -> actionlet task graph for staged rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Action Catalog proto implemented: register, list, version actions
Runtime executes actionlets with idempotency token and returns deterministic result or safe error
Runbook-to-actionlet adapter can convert 10 canonical runbooks into task graphs and run a dry-run simulation
Step-level telemetry: trace IDs emitted, duration, token usage, and outcome (success/fail/safe-fallback)
Console: support engineers can select an actionlet from catalog, provide inputs, and run in 'simulated' and 'live' modes with audit entry created
technical_notes: Design choices: prefer optimistic idempotency (idempotency-token + at-least-once execution with side-effect markers) to keep runtime lightweight; include optional compensating actions for non-idempotent primitives. Persist minimal execution ledger in Dynamo-like store (write-once keys) keyed by idempotency token + action-version. Safety fences: staged approval labels (requires_approval), max-retries with exponential backoff, and a sandboxed dry-run mode that executes simulated effects using stubbed external adapters. Telemetry: emit OpenTelemetry spans per action and attach runbook/step metadata for downstream cost analysis. Rollout plan: start with non-critical runbooks and a feature flag; follow with dedicated operator training and runbook QA checklist.
tasks: Define actionlet schema (inputs, outputs, side_effects, compensator, requires_approval)
Implement registry service with simple CRUD + semantic versioning
Build execution worker supporting idempotency-token ledger and retry policy
Adapter: runbook YAML -> DAG converter (handles parallel/serial steps, conditionals)
UI: simple runner page to pick actionlet, set inputs, and choose dry-run vs live
Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation and send to infra tracing pipeline
Create test-suite with 10 real runbooks (from Support) and smoke CI jobs
comments: 2026-03-02 - Luca Morgan: Initial spike found that several runbook steps are non-idempotent (db-migrations, external account resets). Proposed compensator pattern for those steps to enable safe retries.

2026-03-04 - Anita Sharma: Reviewed schema draft in PR #512; suggested adding 'safety_score' field and 'max_parallel' hint. Assigned follow-up to create mapping from existing runbook step types to actionlet types.

2026-03-07 - SRE (Jing Wei): Asked for retention policy on execution ledger; recommended 90 days hot + archive. Also requested that actionlets emit structured logs with correlation keys for incident reconstruction.
2026-03-10 - PM (Radhika Gupta): Prioritized exposing 'dry-run' mode early for support adoption. Suggested pilot with Billing support team for low-risk workflows.

2026-03-12 - Anita Sharma: Implemented prototype registry and adapter; pushed branch github.com/redwood/ops-reactor/tree/ENG-214501-prototype; ran dry-run of 8/10 pilot runbooks. Observed two steps that need compensators; documented in next-steps.
notes_for_reviewers: Key review points: idempotency ledger design (write amplification tradeoffs), compensator contract, and approval gate UX. Please validate retention and PII protections for any execution inputs (masking needed for secrets).
